Walkthrough · every screen

The current design, in the order a reviewer meets it: opening, reading a step, the Summary, coming back after new commits, and the end of a session. Light and dark, desktop and phone. Sample change: due dates for a small todo app. HANDOFF.md, DESIGN.md and COPY.md describe this page.

Diagram of the flow (design round, not decided)

Recommended shape after research, not yet decided. Only for a step whose change crosses three or more parts or branches: the AI records one diagram with that step, the way it records Look at pointers, and abstains everywhere else. It collapses: it starts closed on every step, as one line under the explanation that names the parts in order; that line opens it and closes it again, its chevron turning, like a file’s (Show or Hide the sequence diagram in its tooltip). Opening and closing animate by grid rows like a file fold; reduced motion snaps. Every arrow cites a line in the diff and goes there when clicked; the arrows this step changed are in ink, the rest muted. A branch shows as UML’s alt box. Up to 5 parts and 7 arrows; a return only when it carries meaning. At 390 the same content is a numbered list. The page draws it from the session’s data, in its own tokens; no Mermaid renderer.

Closed: the parts in order, under the explanation

Syntax colours on every background

Code is coloured as on GitHub: Shiki with github-light and github-dark, each file highlighted whole. The page maps each theme colour to a syntax token, as a class, so nothing needs an inline style. Where GitHub’s colour falls under 4.5:1 on one of the page’s backgrounds, the token is darkened (light) or lightened (dark) in its own hue until it clears all of them; the grid below shows each pair. The changed words inside a changed line keep their wash, made lighter than built so syntax reads on it (decision 27). Colorblind keeps the same syntax tokens: the hues name code, not change.

A file taking its colours

Highlighting never holds the page. The first step’s files are coloured during the Opening, so the walkthrough arrives coloured; the rest are coloured in reading order behind the page, usually before you reach them. If you get there first, the file shows plain (the changed words are already marked: they come from the diff, not the highlighter), and its colours replace the plain text in place when ready: no fade, no spinner, no word, and nothing moves, because the colours change no width. Reduced motion is the same, since there is no motion.

Colorblind

Built in 0.1.5 as “Colour-blind diff”. Kept: a checkbox in the menu’s Theme group, so it works with System, Light and Dark alike. Changed (decision 22): it is named with GitHub’s word, “Colorblind”, and it swaps the whole green and red pair for GitHub’s Protanopia and Deuteranopia blue and orange wherever the pair appears: diff lines, the overview stripe, +/− counts in file headers and the Opening, the desk scene’s code bars, suggestion blocks, criteria and the submitted note. Amber stays amber; every status still has its icon and word. Changed (decision 23): the overview stripe’s marks are drawn at full colour, in both palettes, because the built 55% and 60% fall under 3:1 in light.

The menu: Colorblind sits in the Theme group, under System, Light and Dark

Comments on a whole file

Built in 0.1.5. Kept: GitHub’s “Comment on this file” icon button after Viewed, now on every file header; file threads in a band above the diff, as on GitHub; no suggested change on a file (decision 21); the Summary row names the file with no line. Changed (decision 25): file threads come first in the band and outdated threads after them, since a file thread is about the code on screen; the composer opens at the top of the band, under the button that opened it; the AI may comment on a file, with [AI] and Pending like any of its comments; the Summary row’s tooltip gives the full path.

              Acceptance criteria that say what is missing and where

              Decision 35. Each criterion still shows its icon, the ticket’s words and its status word in the existing colours. Under a partly or not met one: a link like the Summary’s other links to the AI comment that says how to close it (on its lines, or on its file when no line holds it, decision 25), then what is missing in at most 12 words. The comment holds the fix; the row never repeats it. Under a met one: a link to the lines that meet it, which opens them as “Look at” does. Under not checked: why, in at most 8 words. Order: not met, partly met, not checked, met. Picked: met rows stay listed, not folded, because their links are how you check the AI’s “Met”, and a ticket has few criteria.
